conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice; Fock inner products are conjugate-linear in the first variable and linear in the second.

Occupation indices start at zero. Number and factorial operators have the explicitly specified square-summability domains; the normally ordered operator identity initially holds on the finite-particle core.

The invariant measure is dν=d³k/(2|k|), with zero momentum omitted; Wf=f/√(2|k|) converts invariant-measure modes to Lebesgue-measure transverse modes. Wavevector units are inverse metres, and the two mode amplitudes have units metre and metre^(3/2), respectively.

Ideal counts have probabilities p_n=tr(ρP_n). Factorial expectations are spectral sums, without asserting an unbounded trace product. The normalized statistic requires a finite positive mean and finite second factorial moment.
The zero in g^(2)(0) labels a same-mode statistic; no temporal response or pointwise electric-field product is constructed.
Coherent preparations exclude α=0, number preparations require m≥1, and geometric preparations require 0<r<1; orthogonal modes are in vacuum.
Loss means conditionally independent Bernoulli recording with fixed dimensionless efficiency 0<η≤1 and no background or dark counts; the zero-photon fiber uses the empty product one.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, the one-mode occupation projections are mutually orthogonal with strong sum I, define a count PVM, and define a self-adjoint number operator on the stated domain. The diagonal factorial operator M_u=N_u(N_u-I) is self-adjoint, has the finite-particle subspace as a graph core, and is the closure of the finite-particle restriction of a†(u)^2a(u)^2.

Adopt as the ideal detector postulate that this law is the model probability for recording exactly n photons in the selected mode. The detector is number resolving, has unit mode efficiency, and has no mode mismatch, background counts or dark counts.

Under ideal wavepacket counting, the specified coherent-mode vector with α≠0 has g^(2)(0)=1, the number preparation with m≥1 has g^(2)(0)=1−1/m, and the specified geometric one-mode state with 0<r<1 has g^(2)(0)=2.
For the stated incoming count law with 0<μ<∞ and F₂<∞, independent constant-efficiency thinning with 0<η≤1 gives E K=ημ and E[K(K−1)]=η²F₂, hence g_K^(2)(0)=g_N^(2)(0)=g_v^(2)(0).

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit foundational assumption for Hilbert/Fock constructions and the density/PVM probability clauses.
Orthogonal projection values, normalization, multiplicativity, and strong countable additivity of the constructed count PVM.
Second-variable-linear pairing, symmetric Fock sectors, finite-particle subspace, and creation/annihilation formulas.
Equality of adjoint domains and values, closedness of self-adjoint operators, and essential self-adjointness.
Operator equality includes domain equality; graph norms used in the factorial-operator core argument.
Bosonic CCR and finite-particle invariance used to identify the normally ordered factorial operator.
The unitary one-mode factorization and its occupation ladder maps.
Wavevector and length-unit conventions for normalized transverse wavepackets.
The closed transverse subspace of Lebesgue L² and its positive Hermitian pairing.
The adopted positive transverse bosonic free-photon representation; no interacting-QED or empirical conclusion is imported.
Clauses (a) and (b): pure and weighted orthogonal density states and scalar PVM probability laws under Countable Choice. Its additional full-Choice unbounded-moment clause is not used.
Factorial recursion and the index-shifting identities for coherent-state moments.
Finiteness and positivity of the exponential normalization series.
The sum starting at zero equals 1/(1−r) for 0<r<1.
Regrouping nonnegative sums on countable products with sigma-finite counting measures in the geometric-state and thinning calculations.

concerns.concern: The Postulate contains the inline link [[lem-qftx-mode-number-pvm]] despite the statement-first requirement that links appear in the following references section. That supplier is already listed there.

The opening writes H_T=L²(R³,d³k;C³) 'with its transverse condition'. The cited definition instead makes H_T the proper closed subspace satisfying k·f(k)=0 almost everywhere. The qualification indicates the intended space, but the displayed equality should explicitly include that constraint.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier definition and invariant-measure isometry against the counting postulate. Both use dν=d³k/(2|k|), omit zero momentum, impose almost-everywhere transversality, and use Wf=f/√(2|k|) with the second-variable-linear pairing. The consumer needs only this realization and normalization, not rotation or Chern-obstruction conclusions. Neither inspected supplier depends back on the counting page.
